name: Nexthink-Async-MultiResponse-OptionA
description: Option A contact flow for the async multi-response pattern. Uses a Lambda polling loop with DynamoDB as the response queue, a Lex interrupt bot for caller control during hold periods, and Polly/SSML for TTS delivery. This is the proven fallback if Option E's 10-second Lex voice timeout proves insurmountable.
notes: All Lambda invocations in contact flows have an 8-second timeout constraint. Polling and Submit Lambdas are configured with 8s timeout to match.
The Lex interrupt bot uses a 4-second silence timeout. Combined with hold message playback (~3-4s), each polling cycle takes roughly 7-8 seconds.
Contact attributes persist for the call duration and carry state between Lambda invocations (sessionId, cursor, last_response_text, error_count).
This flow has 15+ blocks compared to ~8 for Option E, but uses proven patterns with no platform unknowns.
The polling loop is implemented via branching back to the Invoke Polling Lambda block from multiple downstream blocks.
Consecutive error tracking (3+ errors → inform caller) prevents infinite error loops.

contactAttributes.sessionId: UUID generated by Submit Lambda, persists for the call
contactAttributes.cursor: Last seen sequence number, updated after each successful poll (stringified integer)
contactAttributes.last_response_text: Most recently delivered response text, used for RepeatLastResponse intent
contactAttributes.error_count: Consecutive polling error counter, reset on successful poll, triggers escalation at 3+
contactAttributes.responses_delivered: Total count of responses delivered to caller (for observability)
contactAttributes.session_start_time: Epoch ms when session was created (for duration tracking)

blocks.name: Set Recording & Analytics
blocks.description: Enables Contact Lens analytics for the call. Required for observability and compliance.

blocks.name: Play Welcome
blocks.description: Greets the caller and explains the service.

configuration.text: Welcome to Nexthink IT support. Please describe your question or issue, and I'll look into it for you.

blocks.name: Get Customer Input — Capture Question via Lex
blocks.description: Uses Lex speech recognition to capture the caller's question. The transcribed text is passed to the Submit Lambda.
blocks.notes: A separate Lex bot (not the interrupt bot) captures the initial question. The transcribed text is available as a Lex slot or session attribute.

blocks.name: Invoke Submit Lambda
blocks.description: Submits the caller's question to the Nexthink agent. Creates a session in DynamoDB and POSTs the query with the callback URL.
blocks.notes: The Submit Lambda generates a sessionId (UUID), creates the DynamoDB sentinel record, and POSTs to Nexthink. Returns sessionId and status as contact attributes. 8-second timeout constraint applies.

blocks.name: Check Submission Status
blocks.description: Checks whether the query was successfully submitted to the Nexthink agent.
blocks.notes: On success, the Submit Lambda returns status='submitted' and sessionId. On failure, status='error' with an errorMessage. The sessionId and cursor='0' are set as contact attributes by the Lambda.

blocks.name: Play Acknowledgment
blocks.description: Confirms to the caller that their question is being processed.

configuration.text: I'm looking into that for you. Please hold while I get your answer.

blocks.name: Invoke Polling Lambda
blocks.description: Polls DynamoDB for new responses. This is the entry point of the polling loop — multiple branches route back here.
blocks.notes: The Polling Lambda returns a flat key-value map (contact attributes format): status, responseText, cursor, elapsedSeconds, sessionStatus, isComplete, errorMessage. The 8-second Lambda timeout is the primary constraint — DynamoDB reads must complete well within this window.

blocks.name: Branch on Poll Status
blocks.description: Routes based on the polling result status. This is the main branching point of the polling loop.

conditions.description: No new responses yet, session still active.
Transient error (e.g., DynamoDB read failure). Retry the poll.

blocks.notes: On 'results', the cursor contact attribute has already been updated by the Lambda. On 'waiting', elapsedSeconds is available for timeout decisions. Reset error_count to 0 on any successful poll (results, waiting, or complete).

blocks.name: Play Response via Polly/SSML
blocks.description: Reads the response text to the caller using Amazon Polly with SSML formatting. Stores the response in last_response_text for potential replay.

configuration.ssmlNotes: The Polling Lambda returns pre-formatted SSML with <break> tags between segments (if text was split). The Play Prompt block renders this directly via Polly.

blocks.notes: After playing the response, loop back to poll for more. The cursor was updated by the Polling Lambda, so the next poll will fetch the next undelivered response. Text exceeding 3000 chars is pre-split by the Lambda's TTS utility with SSML break tags.

blocks.name: Play Hold Message
blocks.description: Plays a varied hold message while waiting for responses. The message is selected by the Polling Lambda from a pool of 3+ distinct messages to avoid repetition.

holdMessagePool: I'm still working on getting your answer. Just a moment.
Still looking into that for you. Thanks for your patience.
Your request is being processed. I'll have an update shortly.
configuration.holdMessageNote: The Polling Lambda can return a holdMessage attribute, or the flow can rotate through the pool using a contact attribute counter. Requirement 7.5 mandates no two consecutive messages are the same.

blocks.notes: Hold message playback takes ~3-4 seconds. Combined with the 4-second Lex silence timeout, each wait cycle is ~7-8 seconds total.

blocks.name: Lex Interrupt Bot — Listen for Caller Input
blocks.description: Invokes the AsyncResponseInterruptBot to listen for caller interruptions during the hold period. Uses a 4-second silence timeout — if the caller says nothing, FallbackIntent is returned and polling continues.
blocks.notes: FallbackIntent covers both unrecognized speech AND silence timeout (noinput). All three non-interruption outcomes (FallbackIntent, error, timeout) route back to the polling loop. The 4-second silence timeout is set via the x-amz-lex:audio:start-timeout-ms session attribute per Requirement 5.6.

blocks.name: Handle CancelQuery Intent
blocks.description: Caller wants to cancel the current query. Cleans up the session and offers options.

steps.description: Invoke the Disconnect Lambda to mark the session as ABANDONED.

blocks.name: Handle AskNewQuestion Intent
blocks.description: Caller wants to ask a different question. Abandons the current session and starts a new one.

steps.description: Invoke the Disconnect Lambda to mark current session as ABANDONED before starting a new one.

steps.text: Sure, go ahead and ask your new question.

blocks.notes: Routes back to the initial Get Customer Input block to capture a new question. A new sessionId will be generated by the Submit Lambda.

blocks.name: Handle RepeatLastResponse Intent
blocks.description: Caller wants to hear the last delivered response again.

steps.fallbackText: I don't have a previous response to repeat yet.

blocks.notes: Replays the last_response_text contact attribute. If no response has been delivered yet (attribute is empty), plays a fallback message. Then returns to the polling loop.

blocks.name: Handle Polling Error
blocks.description: Handles transient polling errors. Tracks consecutive errors and escalates after 3+.

blocks.name: Error Escalation — Consecutive Errors
blocks.description: After 3+ consecutive polling errors, inform the caller and offer to end the call.

configuration.text: I'm sorry, I'm having trouble retrieving your results right now. Would you like me to keep trying, or would you prefer to end the call?

blocks.notes: In a full implementation, this would use a Lex bot to capture the caller's decision (keep trying vs. end). For simplicity, this is shown as a branch.

blocks.name: Retry Poll — Transient Error
blocks.description: Plays a brief apology and retries the poll.

blocks.name: Error Decision — Continue or End
blocks.description: Captures the caller's decision after consecutive errors.
blocks.notes: Reuses the interrupt bot. CancelQuery or timeout → end call. FallbackIntent (any other speech) → retry polling. Longer silence timeout (8s) gives the caller time to decide.

blocks.name: Play Completion Message
blocks.description: Informs the caller that all responses have been delivered.

configuration.text: That's everything I have for you on that question.

blocks.name: Ask Another Question
blocks.description: Offers the caller the option to ask another question or end the call.

configuration.text: Would you like to ask another question, or is there anything else I can help with?

blocks.name: Capture Another Question Decision
blocks.description: Listens for the caller's response — either a new question or an indication they're done.
blocks.notes: FallbackIntent (unrecognized speech) is treated as a new question attempt — routes to Get Customer Input. CancelQuery or silence timeout → end call.

blocks.name: Fatal Error
blocks.description: Handles unrecoverable errors (submit failure, initial Lex failure).

configuration.text: I'm sorry, I'm unable to process your request at this time. Please try again later or contact support directly.

blocks.name: End Call
blocks.description: Terminates the contact. A disconnect handler Lambda is triggered separately to mark any active session as ABANDONED.
blocks.notes: The disconnect handler is configured at the contact flow level (not as a block). It invokes a Lambda that calls mark_session_abandoned for the sessionId in the contact attributes.

interruptHandling.CancelQuery: 11a → cleanup session → ask another question or end
interruptHandling.AskNewQuestion: 11b → abandon session → back to Get Customer Input (block 3)
interruptHandling.RepeatLastResponse: 11c → replay last_response_text → back to polling loop

errorHandling.transientErrors: Increment error_count, play brief apology, retry poll
errorHandling.consecutiveErrors_3plus: Inform caller, offer to continue or end

flowSummary.comparisonToOptionE: Option A requires 19 blocks with explicit polling loop, Lex interrupt bot, and error tracking. Option E reduces this to ~8 blocks by delegating all logic to the Orchestrator AI Agent.

lambdaTimeout.impact: All Lambda invocations from the contact flow must complete within 8 seconds. DynamoDB reads in the Polling Lambda must be fast. The Submit Lambda's POST to Nexthink must return quickly (Nexthink returns 202 Accepted immediately).
lambdaTimeout.mitigation: Polling Lambda only reads DynamoDB (fast). Submit Lambda only creates a DynamoDB record and POSTs to Nexthink (which returns 202 immediately). Both operations should complete well within 8 seconds.

lexSilenceTimeout.impact: The Lex interrupt bot listens for 4 seconds of silence before returning FallbackIntent. This is the effective 'wait' period between poll cycles during the hold phase.
lexSilenceTimeout.configuration: Set via x-amz-lex:audio:start-timeout-ms session attribute in the Get Customer Input block.

pollingCycleTime.breakdown: Hold message playback (~3-4s) + Lex silence timeout (4s) = ~7-8s. Plus Lambda invocation overhead (~100-200ms).
pollingCycleTime.note: This means new responses are detected within ~8 seconds of arrival in DynamoDB.

contactAttributeLimits.note: Contact attributes are flat string key-value pairs. The Polling Lambda returns all state as stringified values. Response text stored in last_response_text is limited by the contact attribute size limit.

disconnectHandler.description: A separate Lambda function triggered on caller disconnect. Not a block in the flow — configured at the contact flow level.
disconnectHandler.behavior: Reads sessionId from contact attributes, calls mark_session_abandoned on the session manager.
